newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rewe group retail sales top 50 bln DM in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Rewe group retail sales top 50 bln DM in 1996.

text.p: Privately-controlled German supermarket giant Rewe Handelsgruppe AG last year posted retail turnover of over 50 billion marks ($29.8 billion) for the first time in its history, the company said on Wednesday.
In Germany and abroad, retail sales rose to 50.65 billion marks from 43.13 billion marks. Total sales, including Rewe's wholesale business, rose 16.4 percent to 56.35 billion marks.
"The renewed sales rise of almost eight billion marks strengthens the Rewe group as number one in German and European food retailing," chief executive Hans Reischl said.
Foreign turnover, published by Rewe for the first time, totalled 6.58 billion marks in 1996. Some 1,550 of the group's 11,000 stores are abroad.
Rewe, which last year acquired Austria's Billa supermarket chain, employed 199,000 workers at the end of 1996, up from 168,000 a year earlier.
